hypothesis.statement: In Li₃PX₄ orthothiophosphates and orthophosphates, the Li migration barrier depends mainly on the anion sublattice, not on how the PX₄ tetrahedra are arranged. Swapping O²⁻ for S²⁻ in a fixed framework lowers the barrier substantially, because S²⁻ is more polarizable and screens the moving Li⁺ better at the saddle point, and because it gives a larger, softer lattice with wider Li–Li bottlenecks. The same substitution raises energy above hull, because the oxide is the thermodynamically stronger lattice.
hypothesis.rationale: The notebook is empty, so this is a prior, not a result. The goal asks for a low barrier and stability together, and the usual expectation is that these pull against each other through the anion. If that trade-off is real and anion-driven, later rounds should be organized around anion chemistry. If framework topology matters as much or more, later rounds should search over structure types instead. The test is cheap: Li₃PO₄ and Li₃PS₄ each have two polymorphs forming two isostructural O/S pairs (Pmn2₁ and Pnma), giving a 2×2 anion × framework design that separates the two effects directly. Limits: energy above hull is a proxy for bulk thermodynamic stability, not stability against Li metal. A phase can sit on the hull and still be reduced by Li, as thiophosphates can be toward Li₂S and Li₃P. Reaction energy with Li (or reduction potential) is not a campaign objective, so no Li-metal compatibility will be claimed for any candidate. Barriers come from perfect-crystal, picosecond-scale calculations and say nothing about grain-boundary transport, interphase growth, or real conductivity.
hypothesis.prediction: In both the Pmn2₁ pair and the Pnma pair, the sulfide migration barrier will be at least 0.15 eV lower than the oxide barrier. The anion effect (mean of the two O→S barrier drops) will exceed the framework effect (Pmn2₁ vs Pnma barrier difference at fixed anion, averaged over O and S). Energy above hull (eV/atom) will be higher for the sulfide than for the oxide in each pair.
hypothesis.falsification_criterion: The claim is refuted if, in either isostructural pair, the sulfide barrier is not at least 0.15 eV below the oxide barrier, or if the framework effect is as large as or larger than the anion effect. Separately, if the sulfide energy above hull is equal to or lower than the oxide's in both pairs, the trade-off premise is refuted independently. A pair comparison counts only if both members used the same hopping mechanism (vacancy vs interstitial) and comparable supercell treatment; a mismatched pair is logged as insufficient data and counts as neither support nor refutation. No OOD-flagged barrier may decide the outcome by itself.

batch_plan.strategy: A 2×2 anion × framework design matched by space group, not polymorph label: Li₃PO₄ Pmn2₁ (β), Li₃PS₄ Pmn2₁ (γ), Li₃PO₄ Pnma (γ), Li₃PS₄ Pnma (β). Li₃N P6/mmm is added as a reference baseline on both axes and is not part of the falsification test.

vetoes.reason: Li3N is not a Li3PX4 compound, has no PX4 tetrahedra and no oxide or sulfide analogue in this batch, so it cannot enter either pair, the anion effect or the framework effect of h1. It is a known Li conductor and belongs in its own branch, not this round.

LiN3 is an azide with an N3- molecular anion and covalent N-N bonding, not an orthophosphate or thiophosphate, so it cannot inform h1. Whether the model treats the azide anion reliably is a separate open question and not the basis of this veto.
Li4P2O7 is a pyrophosphate built from corner-sharing P2O7 units, not isolated PO4 tetrahedra, so it is outside the Li3PX4 family. No Li4P2S7 partner is offered, so it cannot form an anion pair.

body.commentary:
Approved: c-mp-13725 (Li3PO4) and c-mp-985583 (Li3PS4), both conditionally. They are the only Li3PX4 candidates and the only ones that can inform h1. Chemistry checks out: P5+ is tetrahedral, Li+ is charge-balanced, and both are retrieved database entries. No duplicates among the five ids.

Condition on the approval: the notebook records only MP ids, not space groups. h1 counts a pair only if both members share a framework (Pmn21 with Pmn21, or Pnma with Pnma). Confirm this from the retrieved structures before counting the two as a pair. If the frameworks differ, the barrier comparison is insufficient data under h1's own rules.

What this batch can test: the prediction needs four structures, Li3PO4 and Li3PS4 in each of Pmn21 and Pnma. This batch supplies at most two, and only if the space-group check passes.
- Framework effect: cannot be computed, because no anion has both frameworks here. The clause "anion effect exceeds framework effect" is insufficient data.
- Barrier clause: at most one pair can be evaluated. A sulfide barrier not at least 0.15 eV below the oxide in that pair would refute h1, since the clause reads "in either pair". A pass is partial support only.
- Energy-above-hull trade-off: refutation requires the sulfide to be equal or lower in both pairs, so one pair can neither refute nor confirm it.
The generator should add the other-framework Li3PO4 and Li3PS4 entries next round. Without them, h1 cannot reach a verdict.

Notes for the Analyst:
- Mechanism and supercell: stoichiometric Li3PX4 has no intrinsic carrier, so each barrier needs an introduced vacancy or interstitial. Check that both pair members used the same mechanism and a comparable supercell size and defect concentration. If they did not, log the pair as insufficient data.
- Upper bound: an NEB-type barrier covers only the hop computed. Unless several distinct hops were sampled, read each barrier as an upper bound on the lowest Li barrier. A failure to reach 0.15 eV could come from sampling a non-optimal sulfide hop, so check how many hops were computed before calling a refutation.
- Scope: these are 0 K single-hop barriers in supercells of at most a few hundred atoms. They are not conductivities or transport activation energies, and they say nothing about grain boundaries, defect formation energy or long-time diffusion.
- Disorder: experimental Pnma Li3PS4 has partially occupied Li sites, so any database entry is an ordered approximant. That is a structure type the method does not treat faithfully, so treat it as OOD. Whether this applies to c-mp-985583 depends on its space group, which is not in the notebook.
- Energy above hull is a weak proxy. It measures decomposition within the compound's own chemical system, not reduction by Li metal. The measurement that would actually test anode stability is missing: the reaction energy with Li, or phase stability at the Li-metal chemical potential. Report it as hull distance only.
- The oxide is referenced to the Li-P-O hull and the sulfide to the Li-P-S hull. A higher sulfide value is testable against the h1 clause as written, but it does not test the stated mechanism ("oxide is the stronger lattice").
- OOD: no measurements exist yet. An OOD-flagged barrier in a pair cannot decide h1 alone and counts only as weak evidence.
